sights.address: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (in front of Blk 28), Singapore
sights.w: Singapore's most iconic surviving 1979 mosaic 'dragon' playground, designed by HDB's Khor Ean Ghee — a terrazzo-tiled dragon head with a climbable ring body. One of only two dragon playgrounds left and a marquee stop on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail.

Singapore's oldest Buddhist monastery — completed 1909 and gazetted a National Monument in 1980 — modelled on Fuzhou's Xi Chan Monastery, with the Hall of Celestial Kings and Mahavira Hall laid out in the classic cong lin ('layered forest') plan.

sights.n: Toa Payoh Town Park & Look-Out Tower
sights.address: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (beside Toa Payoh HDB Hub), Singapore
sights.w: The 4.8-hectare 1970s town park that pioneered greenery in HDB new towns — landscaped ponds, rustic gazebos and the conserved 25 m space-age Look-Out Tower, a favourite 1970s-80s wedding-photo backdrop.
sights.k: Open daily, free; tower not accessible

sights.w: Toa Payoh's first Catholic church (inaugurated 1971), a modernist landmark at the junction of Toa Payoh Central and Lorong 4 that has long offered Mass in English, Mandarin and Tamil — featured on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

The Y-shaped 1967 HDB showpiece with a rooftop viewing gallery once used to survey the young new town from above. Queen Elizabeth II visited in 1972 (as did Princess Anne, Prince Philip and other dignitaries), earning it the 'VIP Block' name.
sights.k: Rooftop gallery closed; view from ground level

sights.w: HDB's headquarters and the civic heart of Singapore's first fully HDB-built satellite town, home to relocated public sculptures — Ng Eng Teng's 'The Climb', Chong Fah Cheong's 'Mama's Precious One' and Ju Ming's 'Tai Chi Boxing' — plus a mall, library and hawker fare.

sights.address: Toa Payoh Central (trail starts near HDB Hub), Singapore
sights.w: NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's second satellite town, linking 16-plus sites — from the Dragon Playground and Town Park to Shuang Lin Monastery — across two themed routes, 'Of Public Housing & Shared Spaces' and 'Of Faiths & Beliefs'.
